transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-21 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sanjay (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Dr. Anika Rao (CTO), Luis Moreno (Infra), Priya Singh (Security), Evan Park (ML Platform)

Summary (auto): Discussed air-gapped on-prem deployment requirements, offline update process, hardware constraints, and pilot timeline.

00:00 Sanjay: hey everybody, thanks for joining, i'm sanjay from redwood inference, maya is our solutions engineer; quick round of intros?
00:12 Anika: hi i'm anika, cto at helix therapeutics. we run genomics pipelines and some ml labs, security is tight so we're exploring airgapped options.
00:20 Luis: luis here, infra lead, we manage the kubernetes clusters and the bare metal racks.
00:26 Priya: priya, head of security, i'll be vetting the install and any kms integrations.
00:32 Maya: great, thanks. objective for today is to understand your constraints — maintenance windows, network egress, hardware, and what success looks like.

02:05 Sanjay: high level questions — are you evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private? looks like you're leaning private airgapped?
02:14 Anika: yes, private on-prem, fully airgapped for PHI and sequencing raw reads. regulatory and compliance reasons, can't have model data leaving our network.
02:30 Maya: ok that maps. for air-gapped we have an offline installer flow — tarballs for images, offline license keys, and an operator that can run without external registry access. do you have a preferred packaging format?
02:46 Luis: we prefer OCI images but often we use tarball images imported into our private registry; also prefer helm charts or an operator manifest we can apply.
03:02 Maya: we support tar import and a signed offline bundle; includes container images, manifests, and a deterministic installer script. installer can be run in an isolated environment.

05:15 Priya: how do you handle secrets and KMS? we use a hardware HSM for key material; we can't export keys.
05:25 Sanjay: we integrate with customer KMS/HSMs — we can support PKCS#11 and external key wrapping. for the air-gapped flow we provide a config to point to on-prem HSM endpoints.
05:39 Priya: is there a requirement to have a Redwood control plane contact back to validate licenses?
05:46 Maya: we can do offline license activation. typical pattern: we ship a time-bounded license file that's signed. renewals happen via an offline token exchange during maintenance windows.
06:10 Anika: good, what about patching and updates? our change windows are monthly and sometimes only at night on weekends.
06:20 Maya: we support staged updates; you can apply operator upgrades during the maintenance window. we also provide delta bundles so you don't need to re-apply large images every time.

08:00 Luis: hardware — we currently have a mix of A100 40GB, A100 80GB, and some older RTX A5000s. interested in running 13B and 70B models. what do you recommend?
08:18 Maya: quick rule of thumb: 13B is fine on A100 40GB with proper quantization and sharding; 70B generally needs 80GB or model parallelism across nodes, or we can use int8 quant with certain kernels. we'll share a sizing sheet.
08:40 Sanjay: do you have prebuilt quantized variants that ship with the installer?
08:46 Maya: yes we can include model variants and a recommended quantization profile. runtime supports automatic kernel selection and optimized paths but note, for air-gapped installs you need compatible GPU drivers and CUDA/CuDNN versions.
09:05 Evan: what's the minimum driver/kernel combo? we run RHEL 8.6 with kernel 4.18, is that ok?
09:12 Maya: that could be tight — many of our optimized paths expect newer kernels; we'll need exact OS and driver versions. we can run in a container compat layer but performance will vary. please list exact distro, kernel, and nvidia driver.

11:30 Priya: auditability — do we get audit logs, per-user tracing and RBAC?
11:36 Sanjay: yes, the private deployment includes audit logs, per-token traces in the console, and fine-grained RBAC tied to your IdP (SAML/SSO). for air-gapped we ship SAML metadata by file and can configure the IdP endpoints internally.
11:55 Priya: any SOC2 / ISO artifacts?
12:00 Sanjay: we'll send the security pack; SOC2, ISO, pentest summary, our RBAC model, and details on data encryption at rest and in transit.

14:10 Anika: latency expectations — some of our clinical pipelines require sub-second for short prompts; is that achievable on-prem?
14:22 Maya: depends on model size and batching. for short prompts on optimized 13B models we can hit sub-second p95 on A100 with the runtime's KV cache and low batch sizes. for chatty pipelines we recommend prefix caching and dedicated pools to avoid cold starts.

16:50 Luis: network topology — we have strict egress control, only specific jump boxes can talk out. how big are the initial images and what's transfer strategy?
17:05 Maya: typical image bundle for the runtime + small model variants is ~20-150GB, large model bundles (70B) are several hundred GB. recommended: transfer via encrypted external drive into an air-gapped zone, or use an internal registry import. we'll provide checksums and signed manifests.

19:40 Anika: operational concerns — who runs the control plane in private deployment? is it us or Redwood?
19:48 Sanjay: we offer two modes: customer-managed control plane (recommended for strict air-gap) or Redwood-managed with a private connector. for Helix, given the constraints, customer-managed control plane looks likely.
20:10 Anika: ok, we prefer customer-managed. what about telemetry, do you require any telemetry back?
20:20 Maya: telemetry is optional — by default we collect anonymized metrics for support; in air-gapped mode we can disable telemetry or ship metrics to your internal observability stack via a prometheus exporter.

22:55 Evan: integration with our ML infra — we use internal model registry and fairing pipelines, do you support model version pinning and rollouts?
23:05 Maya: yes, we support model version pinning, canary rollouts, and automatic fallback to a smaller model variant. rollouts are controlled by config files you store in your gitops repo.

25:30 Priya: do we have to open ports to Redwood for license checks or support shell access?
25:40 Sanjay: no required outbound ports for basic offline usage; for support we can accept a temporary bastion jump from your side or we can provide runbooks for remote debugging. support access is mutually agreed.

28:00 Luis: any constraints on orchestration — we run OpenShift 4.11 and use strict PSPs; will the operator need privileges?
28:14 Maya: operator needs certain elevated permissions for device plugins and node label management; we provide an RBAC manifest scoped to the namespace and documentation for minimal privilege. for OpenShift we have tested manifests.

30:50 Anika: pricing — are there upfront costs for private on-prem?
30:58 Sanjay: yes typically there's a private license fee + pilot SOW for installation and validation; dedicated reserved capacity is different (monthly commit). we'll include SOW and pilot pricing in the follow up.

33:10 Maya: performance benchmarking — we can run a short benchmark harness during the pilot to validate throughput/latency on your hardware and produce a performance profile. that will inform whether you need A100 80GB or can get away with 40GB with sharding.

36:00 Evan: model artifacts — we have custom finetuned weights; do you support bringing-your-own-model (BYOM)?
36:10 Maya: yes, BYOM is supported. for air-gapped we accept model tarballs with manifest, we validate checksum and provide loader hooks. note that for some quant flows we need to run a quantization job — that can be done offline in your environment or we provide pre-quantized artifacts if permitted.

39:20 Priya: legal / procurement — we'll need a DPA, data residency clause, and penalties for breaches. timeline for procurement is about 6-8 weeks after pilot success.
39:34 Sanjay: understood, we'll loop in legal and provide DPA template and references.

42:00 Anika: pilot scope — we'd like a 4-week pilot: install runtime, run benchmarks on 13B model, validate offline updates, integrate with HSM, and test canary rollouts. is that feasible?
42:15 Maya: yes that's a standard pilot. we recommend a small dedicated cluster (2x A100 80GB or 4x A100 40GB) depending on your target models. we'll propose exact node counts in the sizing sheet.

45:30 Luis: maintenance windows — we only have 4 hours on first Saturday of month; can you fit install and upgrades in such windows?
45:40 Maya: installs take longer; for upgrades we support delta bundles and can often fit within short windows; initial install and validation likely need a more extended window or phased approach.

48:10 Sanjay: recap and next steps: we'll send security pack, sizing sheet, pilot SOW and propose workshop dates. Helix to share infra inventory and change window.
48:25 Anika: yep, thanks. any other questions from the team?
48:30 Evan: none from me.
48:33 Priya: nothing else.
48:35 Sanjay: great thanks everyone, we'll follow up by Friday.
48:40 Anika: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
